label: NOTE: what this set reaches, what it cannot, and why one guard has no entry
why: V92Modem's constructor and destructor and t_v92modem.cpp were written by one hand at one sitting from one reading of .text+0x13d30-0x13eb8 and +0x13990-0x13a74. Every entry below is a claim the disassembly makes: the two diagnostic lines and the two `> 1` gates on each, the five sysdep_malloc immediates, the two argument stores, the three arms of the switch, the seven arguments of the V92Modulator call, the five releases and the ONE nulling. THREE CLAIMS HAVE A CHECK OF THEIR OWN BECAUSE THE POINTER THEY LIVE BEHIND CANNOT AGREE: every allocation size (compared as harness_alloc.bytes against the reference, which is the only witness the ten arrays inside the parameter block have), the seven modulator arguments (compared by ADDRESS on both sides, since two constructors making the same mistake would agree), and the destructor's single store (spelled as `+0x008 is zero afterwards exactly when it was not before, and nothing else moved'). WHAT NO ENTRY HERE CAN REACH, and each for a stated reason. (1) `if (mappingParams)' in the destructor: V92deleteConstellations dereferences the same pointer two calls earlier with no null test of its own, so the guard's false branch is unreachable in the OBJECT and deleting the guard is behaviourally identical on every input that does not fault both sides -- finding 1322, and this is why the subset sweep is over four pointers and not five. (2) The ORDER of the five releases: the harness allocator counts frees and does not sequence them, exactly as v92mod.json records for the eleven. (3) The switch reading the MEMBER rather than the parameter: the two are the same value at that point and the difference is an instruction, not a behaviour. (4) The fifth argument, V92ComputationalMode: no entry can make a function read a value it must not read, so it is swept as data instead -- varied per trial, same on both sides.
